A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same adaptive elicitation framework. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: Sections 3–4 and Appendices C–D report original experiments on Twenty Questions, OpinionQA, and EEDI, including prediction, calibration, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their reported prediction, calibration, and ablation results.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same autoregressive meta-training, question–answer permutation, answer-token masking, greedy expected-information-gain selection, and Monte Carlo planning. The revised explanations do not change these procedures.

E1.justification: Twenty Questions, OpinionQA, EEDI, and the rare-answer evaluation scenarios are retained. The dataset newly highlighted in v2's introduction was already constructed and evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The Base LLM and in-context tuning baselines remain unchanged. Figures 5–6 also retain the same random/EIG/MCTS comparisons and Base/ICT/meta-trained model comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain the 70/15/15 entity splits, training settings, 20 candidate questions and five targets, and accuracy, perplexity, calibration-error, and Brier-score metrics. The ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: The calibration analyses, rare-answer subgroup analysis, training/planning ablation, and target-count, candidate-count, and model-size ablations remain unchanged in Sections 4.2–4.5 and Appendices C–D.

E5.justification: The stated 10,000 evaluation trials and averaging practice are unchanged. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 3–9 retain identical plotted data, and Tables 1–3 retain all numerical entries. For example, Table 3 still reports accuracies of 0.5201, 0.6131, and 0.7382. Changed plot images only update the Twenty Questions name.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces an unconditional equality in the maximum-likelihood/KL-divergence argument with an inequality and explicitly qualifies equality by the model class containing the true distribution. The propositions and Appendix A proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: The framework, uncertainty-reduction, and empirical superiority claims remain the same. v2 emphasizes the Twenty Questions contribution in the introduction, but its construction and public release were already claimed in v1 Section 3.1.

C2.justification: Section 2.3 newly acknowledges that question-order independence can be unrealistic. Section 2.5 more explicitly connects simulator mismatch to poor generalization, although its new description of the bound's second moment as a variance is imprecise.

D1.justification: Implementation settings and resource access information are retained. The code and dataset links repeated in v2's introduction were already supplied in v1's Reproducibility section and Section 3.1.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain unchanged. v2 consolidates duplicate Chaloner and Verdinelli references from 1995a/1995b into one entry; this does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: v2 edits methodological prose, rewrites and retitles Section 2.5, moves detailed proposition explanations to Appendix A, and standardizes Twenty Questions terminology. It also adds the ICML publication note while retaining the overall document structure.

P2.justification: All nine figures and three tables remain. v2 updates plot titles and captions, relocates Figures 2–3, and regroups appendix figures and tables. Displayed data and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected model-class qualification in Section 2.3 and explicit question-order limitation modestly improve rigor and transparency, alongside editorial clarification. The empirical evidence is preserved. The new variance wording in Section 2.5 introduces a localized imprecision, but does not outweigh these limited improvements.
